# Can AMP generate any usable skill automatically from motion clips alone?

> **Current answer:** AMP trains a discriminator on unstructured motion clips to produce a style reward and combines it with a task reward, reducing per-skill handcrafted imitation objectives. Its capability remains limited by data coverage, task definition, mode collapse, and the simulation-to-real gap; it is not a pipeline that turns any video into a deployable robot skill.

## Key terms

- Reinforcement Learning (强化学习, RL)
- Simulation-to-Real (仿真到现实, Sim2Real)

## Applicable robots

- Simulated characters; not evidence from a physical humanoid.

## Applicable simulators

- Isaac Gym.

## Controllers and methods

- Adversarial motion prior with a reinforcement-learning policy.

## Applicable environments

- Physics-based character simulation tasks reported in the paper.

## Assumptions

- Motion data covers the required style and relevant state transitions.
- Discriminator collapse, reward exploitation, and policy learning are monitored separately.

## Result

- AMP trains a discriminator on unstructured motion clips to produce a style reward and combines it with a task reward, reducing per-skill handcrafted imitation objectives. Its capability remains limited by data coverage, task definition, mode collapse, and the simulation-to-real gap; it is not a pipeline that turns any video into a deployable robot skill.

## Limitations

- Motion data covers the required style and relevant state transitions.
- Discriminator collapse, reward exploitation, and policy learning are monitored separately.
